structure: Part 2 read, in full, the 15 named files of src/server/app/shared/ (layout.njk, kit.js, save-actions.njk, error-summary.njk, error.njk, section-caption.njk, render-macro.js, copy.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, copy-leaves.js, paths.js, paging.js, trail.js, set-context.js), the six files of src/server/app/page-maturity/ (banner.njk, levels.js, page-maturity.js, _banner.scss and the English and Welsh copy), both shared search components under src/server/common/components/ (accessible-autocomplete and multi-select-search, each with macro.njk, its SCSS and its README), the client bundle (src/client/javascripts/application.js and its six component modules: accessible-autocomplete, autocomplete-text, multi-select-search, transporter-filter, region-code-prefix, status-announcer), the three client helpers (search-fold, bold-matches, welsh-results-available), the SCSS entry application.scss with its two core partials, seven component partials and two helper partials, and the type-ahead FIT spec src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/type-ahead.fit.spec.js. It covered the chrome every page shares rather than any one page: the GOV.UK page template the service extends, the service name, header, Alpha phase banner, service navigation and footer, the page-title and section-caption patterns, the Back link and the `from` trail it follows, the Save and continue / Save and return to overview / Cancel and return to overview controls, the error summary and inline field errors, the recoverable-error, stale-action and success banners, the journey status strip, the page-maturity banner and its four levels, every key of the shared English copy module with a parity claim for the Welsh one, the two shared search components with their client-side JavaScript, announcements and SCSS, each custom SCSS partial and the GOV.UK component it extends, the shared paging helper, the set-mounted URL shapes, and every behaviour the type-ahead FIT spec proves with JavaScript on and off. Two files outside the slice are named only where a file read here depends on them: the submitted-search macro the multi-select-search macro imports, and src/config/config.js for the maturity banner's switch. Welsh copy was read for key parity, not claimed string by string.

claims.statement: Every page of the service is rendered inside the GOV.UK page template, so the GOV.UK skip link, header, width container, main wrapper and footer surround the service's own content.
claims.quote: {% extends "govuk/template.njk" %}

claims.statement: The service is named "Import notification service" wherever a page names it.
claims.quote: serviceName: 'Import notification service'

claims.statement: A page's browser title reads the page's own title, then the service name, then GOV.UK, separated by hyphens.
claims.quote: {% block pageTitle %}{% if errorSummary %}{{ sharedCopy.layout.errorTitlePrefix }}{% endif %}{{ pageTitle }} - {{ sharedCopy.layout.serviceName }} - {{ sharedCopy.layout.govukSuffix }}{% endblock %}

claims.statement: A page showing an error summary has "Error: " in front of its browser title.
claims.quote: errorTitlePrefix: 'Error: '

claims.statement: The GOV.UK header's crown links to https://www.gov.uk/ and the header sits in the GOV.UK width container.
The header's bottom border is a light grey rather than the GOV.UK default.
claims.note: look and feel only; the GOV.UK header component is otherwise unchanged

claims.statement: The service navigation shows its links only to a signed-in user; a page shown to anyone else carries the service name alone.
claims.quote:
{% set navigationItems = [] %}
  {% if userSession and userSession.isAuthenticated %}

claims.statement: The service navigation offers four links, in this order: Dashboard, Address book, Manage account, Log out.
claims.quote:
serviceNavigation: {
      menuButton: 'Menu',
      dashboard: 'Dashboard',
      addressBook: 'Address book',
      manageAccount: 'Manage account',
      logOut: 'Log out'
    }

claims.statement: The Dashboard navigation link points at the page's home URL and is marked as the current page when the page says the dashboard is the active navigation item.
claims.quote:
text: sharedCopy.layout.serviceNavigation.dashboard,
        href: homeUrl,
        active: activeNavigationItem == "dashboard"

claims.statement: The Log out navigation link signs the user out at /auth/sign-out.
claims.quote: {% set signOutUrl = "/auth/sign-out" %}

claims.statement: The Manage account navigation link leads nowhere: its href is a bare fragment.
claims.quote: {% set manageAccountUrl = "#" %}
claims.note: the link is shown to every signed-in user but takes them to no page

claims.statement: At narrow widths the navigation collapses behind a button labelled "Menu".
claims.quote: menuButtonText: sharedCopy.layout.serviceNavigation.menuButton

claims.statement: The service name in the navigation links to the page's home URL, which on a journey page is the set's own notification list.
claims.quote:
serviceName: sharedCopy.layout.serviceName,
    serviceUrl: homeUrl,
claims.note: homeUrl is dashboardPath() for a journey page and '/' for a page outside any set

claims.statement: Every page carries a phase banner with a grey "Alpha" tag reading "This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email."
The phase banner's feedback link opens an email to the APHA service desk.
claims.quote: {% set feedbackUrl = "mailto:APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk" %}

claims.statement: The footer offers three links: Privacy, Cookies and Accessibility statement, each to the matching page on gov.uk.
claims.quote:
href: "https://www.gov.uk/help/privacy-notice",
          text: sharedCopy.layout.footer.privacy
claims.note: the copy keys are privacy: 'Privacy', cookies: 'Cookies', accessibility: 'Accessibility statement'

claims.statement: A Back link labelled "Back" shows above the page content, and only on a page that supplies somewhere for it to go.
A page's content is two-thirds of the page width by default, the reading measure for a form.
claims.quote: <div class="{{ contentColumnClass | default("govuk-grid-column-two-thirds", true) }}">

claims.statement: A page that displays rather than asks can render across the full page width.
claims.note: only these two widths exist; a page names one of them

claims.statement: A page asking for a width the service does not offer fails rather than rendering at a default width.
claims.note: mechanism: guards the page's own width choice, not anything a trader sees

claims.statement: When a save fails for a reason the trader can wait out, the page shows a notification banner titled "There is a problem" saying "Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes."
claims.note: the banner is announced: role is alert, and a page may replace the body

claims.statement: When an action is refused because the notification changed since the page was opened, the page shows a banner titled "The notification has been updated" saying "This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again."
A journey page shows a status strip above its content holding the notification's status tag and its reference in bold.
claims.quote: {{ govukTag({ text: journeyStrip.status.text, classes: journeyStrip.status.classes }) }} {{ journeyStrip.reference }}
claims.note: a page may leave the strip off

claims.statement: The status strip's tag reads Draft in blue, Submitted in green, Amend in yellow or Deleted in grey.
claims.quote:
journeyStrip: {
    draft: 'Draft',
    submitted: 'Submitted',
    amend: 'Amend',
    cancelAmend: 'Cancel amend',
    deleted: 'Deleted'
  }
claims.note: classes are govuk-tag--blue, --green, --yellow and --grey in that order

claims.statement: While a notification is being amended, every journey page offers a "Cancel amend" link in the status strip, going to the notification's cancel-amend page.
claims.quote:
export const cancelAmendControl = (journey) =>
  journey.status === AMEND
    ? {
        href: pagePath(journey.journeyId, CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG),
        text: sharedCopy.journeyStrip.cancelAmend
      }
    : undefined
claims.note: a page may suppress the link with offerCancelAmend false

claims.statement: A page may open with a green success banner carrying its own title and message.
Every page carries a cross-site request forgery token in a meta tag, so a form posted from the page can be checked as coming from it.
claims.quote: <meta name="csrf-token" content="{{ crumb }}">

claims.statement: The service's stylesheet loads in the head and its JavaScript loads as a module at the end of the body, so a page is rendered and usable before any script runs.
claims.quote: <script type="module" src="{{ getAssetPath('application.js') }}"></script>

claims.statement: An error page shows a large heading and a single paragraph of explanation, inside the same chrome as every other page.
claims.quote:
{{ heading }}

{{ message }}

claims.statement: The service has five error-page messages: "Page not found", "Forbidden", "You need to sign in to view this page", "There is a problem with your request" and "Something went wrong".
claims.quote:
errorPage: {
    notFound: 'Page not found',
    forbidden: 'Forbidden',
    unauthorized: 'You need to sign in to view this page',
    badRequest: 'There is a problem with your request',
    unexpected: 'Something went wrong'
  }

claims.statement: A user the service cannot sign in is told "Sorry, we are unable to sign you in." and offered a link to try again.
A page names the section of the journey it belongs to in a caption above its heading, in the large GOV.UK caption size, and shows nothing when the page has no section.
A journey page's caption is the caption of the journey section its page belongs to, and a page the journey leaves uncaptioned shows none.
claims.quote: caption: journeySectionCaption(page?.id),
claims.note: the section captions themselves belong to the journey flow, not to this part

claims.statement: A journey page's primary button reads "Save and continue".
claims.quote: saveAndContinue: 'Save and continue'

claims.statement: A journey page offers a secondary button reading "Save and return to overview" beside Save and continue.
claims.quote:
text: copy.saveAndReturnToHub,
        classes: "govuk-button--secondary",
        name: "exit",
        value: "hub"

claims.statement: A journey page offers a link below its buttons reading "Cancel and return to overview", going to the notification's overview.
claims.quote: {{ copy.cancelAndReturnToHub }}

claims.statement: A page can leave out both return controls, showing only its primary button.
claims.quote: {% set showReturnControls = params.showReturnControls if params.showReturnControls is defined else true %}

claims.statement: A page can add one more secondary button of its own beside the save controls, posting its own name and value.
On a page that takes a file, every save button posts the form to the upload path as multipart, so a chosen file is sent whichever save the trader presses.
claims.quote: {% set fileAttributes = { formaction: uploadPath, formenctype: "multipart/form-data" } if uploadPath else {} %}

claims.statement: A page can put a hidden implicit-submit control ahead of its other buttons so pressing Enter in a field activates the control the page intends rather than the first button on the page.
claims.quote: <button type="submit"{% if params.name %} name="{{ params.name }}" value="{{ params.value }}"{% endif %} class="govuk-visually-hidden" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">{{ params.text }}</button>
claims.note: the control is hidden from assistive technology and out of the tab order

claims.statement: A refused page shows an error summary titled "There is a problem".
The error summary lists one entry per field in error, in the order the page's error map gives them, and each entry links to that field on the page.
claims.quote: errorList: entries.map(([field, text]) => ({ text, href: href(field) }))
claims.note: the default link is the in-page anchor #<field>; a page may supply its own builder when the entries point at another page

claims.statement: No error summary is shown when a page has no errors.
A page that shows an error summary without the trader having just been refused can keep the caret where it is instead of moving it to the summary.
claims.quote: disableAutoFocus,

claims.statement: A field in error also shows its message inline against the field itself, the same words the summary carries.
claims.quote:
export const fieldError = (fieldErrors, field) =>
  fieldErrors?.[field] ? { text: fieldErrors[field] } : undefined

claims.statement: Pressing Save and return to overview on any journey page takes the trader to that notification's overview.
Pressing Save and continue takes the trader to the next page of the journey that applies to the notification, and to the review page when no page is left.
When the next page needs a required earlier answer the notification does not have, Save and continue opens the page that asks for that answer instead.
claims.quote: 'Save and continue opened the page that asks for a missing earlier answer'
claims.note: logged once with the saved page, the unopened page and the missing answer ids

claims.statement: The review page of a notification is reached at the slug notification-view, and the page that abandons an amendment at the slug cancel-amend.
claims.quote:
export const CYA_SLUG = 'notification-view'

export const CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG = 'cancel-amend'

claims.statement: A refusal is recorded once in the service's logs with the keys of the fields refused, never the messages the trader was shown.
claims.quote: errorCodes: Object.keys(fieldErrors)
claims.note: mechanism: logging of refusals; the log message is 'Answer refused, page shown again'

claims.statement: When a save fails on a backend error the trader can wait out, the page answers with its own fallback and the failure is recorded once as a warning.
claims.quote:
export const SAVE_FALLBACK_LOG_MESSAGE =
  'Save failed on a recoverable backend error, fallback response sent'

claims.statement: A post refused because the notification changed since the page was shown sends the trader back to the same page carrying a staleAction marker, which is what raises the "The notification has been updated" banner.
claims.quote:
query.set('staleAction', '1')
      return h.redirect(`${request.path}?${query.toString()}`)

claims.statement: Every journey page carries the notification's concurrency token, so a post can be refused when the notification has moved on.
claims.quote: concurrencyToken: journey?.concurrencyToken ?? null,

claims.statement: A page's Back link goes to the place the trader actually came from, carried between pages in a `from` query parameter listing those places newest last.
claims.quote:
export const TRAIL_PARAMETER = 'from'
export const TRAIL_SEPARATOR = ','

claims.statement: A trail can start from three places outside the journey's pages: the notification's overview, the set's notification list, and the INS type question.
Back goes to the notification's overview when the page carries no trail.
claims.quote: const fallbackHref = fallback ?? hubPath(journeyId)
claims.note: a page may name a different fallback

claims.statement: A trail naming anywhere the journey does not have is ignored in full, Back falls back, and the trail is recorded once as a warning with at most 200 characters of what was received.
claims.quote: 'Trail not recognised, trail dropped'

claims.statement: A trail holds at most 40 places; a longer one loses its oldest.
claims.quote: export const LONGEST_TRAIL = 40

claims.statement: A sub-page opened from another page returns to that page when the request carries a `return` marker naming a page allowed to open it; a marker naming anything else is ignored and recorded once as a warning.
claims.quote: 'Return marker not recognised, marker dropped'

claims.statement: A date hint on any page reads "For example, 27/3/2026".
claims.quote: dateExample: 'For example, 27/3/2026'

claims.statement: Where an answer does not apply, the service shows "Not applicable".
claims.quote: notApplicable: 'Not applicable'

claims.statement: The actions a trader can take on a notification are named "Copy as new" and "Delete", and a deletion confirms with "Notification deleted" and "The notification has been deleted."

Where a journey page lets the trader add an address to the address book, the control reads "Add a new address" and a success banner titled "Success" says the named address was added to your address book.

When an address chosen on a journey page is no longer in the address book the page says "The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.", and when the address book cannot be reached it says "The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes."

Unless a field says otherwise, the service's validation messages are "Select a valid option", "Enter a valid postcode", "Enter a valid registration number", "Enter a valid UK telephone number", "Enter a valid date", "Enter a real time, like 14:30" and "Enter a whole number".
claims.quote:
export const validatorDefaults = {
  oneOf: 'Select a valid option',
  postcode: 'Enter a valid postcode',
  vehicleReg: 'Enter a valid registration number',
  ukPhone: 'Enter a valid UK telephone number',
  date: 'Enter a valid date',
  time: 'Enter a real time, like 14:30',
  wholeNumber: 'Enter a whole number',

claims.statement: An answer over a field's length limit is refused with "Enter <limit> characters or fewer", and a number outside a field's range with "Enter a number between <low> and <high>".
claims.quote:
maxLength: (max) => `Enter ${max} characters or fewer`,
  numberBetween: (min, max) => `Enter a number between ${min} and ${max}`

claims.statement: Every shared string has a Welsh counterpart: the Welsh shared copy module carries the same key tree as the English one, with no key missing and none extra, and the same two parameterised messages.
claims.quote: serviceName: 'Gwasanaeth hysbysu mewnforio',
claims.note: checked key by key: layout (serviceName, errorTitlePrefix, govukSuffix, back, phaseBanner.tag/bodyPrefix/feedbackLinkText, serviceNavigation.menuButton/dashboard/addressBook/manageAccount/logOut, footer.privacy/cookies/accessibility), unauthorised, errorSummary, recoverableError, dateExample, notApplicable, errorPage, staleActionRejected, notificationActions, saveActions, journeyStrip, addressHandshake, and validatorDefaults

claims.statement: The Welsh copy is machine-drafted and not fit to be shown to the public until a translator and Welsh Language Standards sign-off have passed it.
claims.quote: // MACHINE-DRAFT Welsh — not reviewed by a translator. Do not ship user-facing without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.

claims.statement: A page is shown in English, and in Welsh only where the caller asks for it; an unknown language falls back to English.
claims.quote:
export const copyFor = (locales, locale = DEFAULT_LOCALE) =>
  locales[locale] ?? locales[DEFAULT_LOCALE]

claims.statement: A trader cannot yet choose Welsh: nothing picks a language from a cookie or a toggle, so every page renders in English.
claims.quote:
Only `en` exists
 * until a second language is commissioned; locale selection (cookie,
 * language toggle) plugs in via the `locale` argument when it is.
claims.note: the Welsh modules exist but no request path passes a locale

claims.statement: Every page shows how settled its design is, as a second phase banner under the Alpha one.
claims.quote: {% include "page-maturity/banner.njk" %}

claims.statement: The four design states a page can be in read "Exploring" ("This page is an early idea. It may change a lot or be removed."), "Detailing" ("We're keeping this page. We're still working out the detail."), "Agreed" ("Users and the business have agreed this page. Changes need a reason.") and "Ready for live" ("This page is ready for live.").
The maturity tag is orange for Exploring, purple for Detailing, teal for Agreed and green for Ready for live, and the banner row behind it takes the same colour at a lighter tint.
claims.note: the row's colour is the 50% tint and the banner colour runs 10px past the content edge

claims.statement: A page that says nothing about how settled it is shows as Exploring.
claims.quote: return page.maturity ?? LEVELS.exploring

claims.statement: The maturity banner is left off an error page and off any response that is not a page of the journey, and the whole banner can be switched off for an environment, though it is on by default.
claims.note: the switch is PAGE_MATURITY_BANNER_ENABLED and defaults to true

claims.statement: A screen reader hears "This page's status:" before the maturity tag, and a full stop after it, so the tag is not read as part of the sentence that follows.
claims.quote: {{ pageMaturity.hiddenPrefix }} {{ pageMaturity.tag.text }}.

claims.statement: The maturity banner has Welsh copy for the prefix and all four states, with the same keys as the English.
claims.quote: hiddenPrefix: 'Statws y dudalen hon:',

claims.statement: A long list the trader must pick one entry from is shown as a search box that suggests as they type, and as a plain list to choose from when JavaScript does not run.
claims.quote:
`appAccessibleAutocomplete` turns a native `govukSelect` into a type-ahead. The
select stays in the page as the control that posts; the script enhances it when
JavaScript runs, and without JavaScript the trader uses the plain select.

claims.statement: A page using the search box sets how many characters are typed before matches show, the message when nothing matches, the language, whether the whole list shows on focus, whether the first match is highlighted, a value to start with, and the text in the empty box.
claims.quote:
autocomplete.minLength     (int)     characters before matches show
    autocomplete.noResults     (string)  message when nothing matches
    autocomplete.language      (string)  'en' (default) or 'cy'
    autocomplete.showAllValues (bool)    show the full list on focus
    autocomplete.autoselect    (bool)    highlight the first match
    autocomplete.defaultValue  (string)  value to prefill the input with
    autocomplete.placeholder   (string)  text shown in the empty search box

claims.statement: A search box a page says nothing more about suggests from the first character typed, in English, with no placeholder, no starting value, no highlighted first match and the whole list hidden until the trader types.
claims.quote:
"data-min-length": ac.minLength if ac.minLength is defined else 0,
      "data-language": ac.language if ac.language else "en",
      "data-show-all-values": "true" if ac.showAllValues else "false",
      "data-auto-select": "true" if ac.autoselect else "false",

claims.statement: The suggestions are the entries of the list itself; the list's own "choose one" entry is never suggested.
claims.quote:
The suggestions are the select's options that carry a value. The option with
  an empty value is the select text and is never suggested.

claims.statement: A search matches an entry anywhere in its words, ignoring capitals and accents, so typing "frâ" or "fra" both find France.
claims.quote:
export const containsTerm = (text, term) =>
  foldForSearch(text).includes(foldTerm(term))

claims.statement: Each suggestion shows the letters the trader typed in bold, with the accented letters of a name marked as a whole where an unaccented search matched them.
claims.quote: const strongMatch = (text) => `${escapeHtml(text)}`
claims.note: the text is escaped before the bold is added, so an entry's own characters cannot inject markup

claims.statement: Choosing a suggestion, or leaving the box on a name that matches an entry exactly, picks that entry.
claims.quote:
const chosen = chosenOption ?? enhancedInputFor(inputId)?.value
    replaceSelectionWithOptionNamed(selectElement, selectOptions, chosen)

claims.statement: Picking an entry announces the change once, and only when the answer actually changed, so a page that reveals more questions from the answer reveals them once.
The field's hint and error message are announced with the search box, because the description moves onto the box the trader actually types in.
claims.quote:
enhanced.setAttribute(
      ARIA_DESCRIBEDBY,
      `${describedBy} ${enhancedDescribedBy}`.trim()
    )

claims.statement: A search box carries a square blue magnifier button joined flush to its right-hand edge, which is decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology, is not in the tab order, and only puts the caret in the box.
claims.quote:
const button = document.createElement('span')
  button.className = BUTTON_CLASS
  button.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true')
  button.addEventListener('click', () => input.focus())

claims.statement: The search box's assistive hint reads "When autocomplete results are available use up and down arrows to review and enter to select. Touch device users, explore by touch or with swipe gestures."
claims.quote:
export const ENGLISH_ASSISTIVE_HINT =
  'When autocomplete results are available use up and down arrows to review and enter to select. Touch device users, explore by touch or with swipe gestures.'

claims.statement: In Welsh the search box's assistive hint, its too-short, no-results, result-count and highlighted-option announcements are all given in Welsh.
claims.quote:
tStatusQueryTooShort: (minQueryLength) =>
    `Ysgrifennwch ${minQueryLength} neu fwy o gymeriadau am ganlyniadau`,

claims.statement: The Welsh result count is given in the singular for one result and the plural for any other number.
claims.quote:
export const welshResultsAvailable = (count) =>
  `${count} ${count === 1 ? 'canlyniad' : 'o ganlyniadau'} ar gael`

claims.statement: The search box and its suggestions are set in GOV.UK typography at the body size, the box takes the GOV.UK focus style when focused and the GOV.UK error border when the answer was refused, and the library's own dropdown arrow is hidden.
The search box behaviour is adapted from HMRC Frontend's accessible-autocomplete at a pinned commit under the Apache 2.0 licence, so its notice must stay with the code.
claims.quote:
Adapted from HMRC Frontend's accessible-autocomplete component:
 *   https://github.com/hmrc/hmrc-frontend
 *   src/components/accessible-autocomplete/accessible-autocomplete.js
 *   Pinned commit: 8aba9fc0b60a193d69fea0d3435a5b504cb922c4

claims.statement: Where the trader picks several things across several searches, the page offers a search box whose results they tick; without JavaScript the Search button posts the page and the server renders the results again, and with JavaScript the results refresh in place with nothing reloading.
claims.quote:
Without JavaScript it is a submitted
search: the Search button posts the page's form with `action=search`, and the
server renders the page again with the results. With JavaScript the results
refresh in place as the trader types, ticks, removes or clears, and nothing
reloads.

claims.statement: The multi-select search box is a search field with the browser's own autofill off, says which part of the page its results are in, and has a hidden live region for announcing them.
claims.note: the box itself comes from the submitted-search macro, which this part did not read

claims.statement: The matching, ordering, labels, bold text and validation of a multi-select search are all worked out on the server, because the same page renders the results whether JavaScript runs or not.
claims.quote:
Because the page renders the results on both paths, the matching, the order,
the labels, the bold text and the validation each have one owner, on the
server.

claims.statement: Typing in a multi-select search refreshes the results once the trader pauses for a quarter of a second; ticking or unticking a result refreshes them straight away.
claims.quote: const typingDelayMs = 250

claims.statement: Refreshes of a multi-select search run one at a time, each posted only once the one before it has landed, so two never reach the server at once and a search pressed straight after Clear all does not post the cleared choices again.
claims.quote:
Refreshes run one at a time. Each is posted only once the one before it has
  landed, from the form that one left

claims.statement: Saving straight after a tick, a Remove or Clear all saves what the trader can see: a button outside the search waits for any refresh still in flight, and a typed search still waiting on the pause is dropped.
claims.quote:
If refreshes are still on their way, the submit waits for them to land,
  so a save pressed straight after Clear all or a Remove saves what the trader
  sees. A typed search still waiting for the trader to pause is dropped.

claims.statement: After the results refresh, the keyboard stays where it was: focus returns to the same control, moves to the search box when that control has gone, and is left alone when the trader has moved it elsewhere.
claims.quote:
After a swap, focus goes back to the element with the same id. If that element
  has gone, such as a Remove button, focus moves to the search box. If the
  trader has moved focus elsewhere while the results refreshed, it stays there.

claims.statement: A screen reader is told about the results after a typed search or a press of Search, and told nothing after a tick, a Remove or Clear all.
claims.quote:
After a typed search or a Search press, the live region reads the response's
  announcement. A tick, a Remove or Clear all announces nothing.
claims.note: the words announced are the page's own copy, carried on the response

claims.statement: If a refresh of the results fails or cannot reach the server, the page posts itself instead, so the trader carries on with the version that needs no JavaScript.
claims.quote:
When the results route fails or cannot be reached, the script submits the
  form with the button that started the refresh, so the trader gets the page
  without JavaScript.

claims.statement: Escape in the search box, or a click outside the search, hides the results list and keeps what the trader typed; focusing or clicking the box shows it again, and each refresh shows the new results.
claims.quote:
Escape in the search box hides the dropdown and keeps the term, because the
  browser's own Escape would clear a search box.
claims.note: the list hides on the click rather than the press, so the layout does not move under a button being clicked

claims.statement: A multi-select search shows an "update" button under the results for traders without JavaScript, because a tick alone cannot post the page, and that button is hidden once the script is running.
claims.quote:
`__update` is a button under the results for use without JavaScript, such as
  "Add selection" posting `action=search`. A tick cannot post the form
  without a script, so this is how the chips catch up.

claims.statement: The results of a multi-select search are a bordered list joined to the bottom of the search box that scrolls once it passes 270 pixels, with 44-pixel striped tick-box rows under a bold group heading, and what has been chosen shows beneath as a count with Clear all beside it and one chip per choice carrying a cross to remove it.
claims.note: the whole search is at most 630px wide; a hovered small tick box loses the ring GOV.UK draws, keeping only the focus ring

claims.statement: A page's results route for a multi-select search never saves the trader's choice: only the page's own save does.
claims.quote:
It never saves the trader's choice: only the

claims.statement: A list of transporters filters down to the rows holding what the trader types, as they type, with the matching letters in bold, and shows a no-matches message in place of the table when nothing matches.
claims.quote:
table.hidden = shown.length === 0
      noMatches.hidden = shown.length > 0
claims.note: filtering is in the browser over rows already on the page, and the Search button filters without posting

claims.statement: A screen reader is told how many transporter rows are showing after each filter, and told the no-matches message when none are.
claims.quote:
liveRegion.textContent = shownCount
        ? messages[shownCount - 1]

claims.statement: A transporter search term already on the page filters the rows as soon as the page loads, without announcing anything.
Where a page shows the dialling or region prefix that goes with a country, the prefix changes as soon as the trader changes the country, and is blank for a country with none.
A message a page wants a screen reader to read on arrival is announced a moment after the page loads rather than with it, so the reader notices it.
claims.quote: const ANNOUNCE_DELAY_MS = 150

claims.statement: Where JavaScript runs, the pages get the GOV.UK button, tick box, error summary, radio, service navigation and skip-link behaviours, the Ministry of Justice date picker, and the service's own five enhancements.
claims.quote:
createAll(Button)
createAll(Checkboxes)
createAll(ErrorSummary)
createAll(Radios)
createAll(ServiceNavigation)
createAll(SkipLink)
createAll(DatePicker)
claims.note: the only non-GOV.UK library is @ministryofjustice/frontend, for the date picker

claims.statement: Anything a page can only offer with JavaScript is hidden when the GOV.UK JavaScript has not run, so a trader without it is never shown a control that would do nothing.
A control that posts can be shown as a link, in the GOV.UK link colours including hover and active, so an action needing a form still reads as a link.
claims.note: used by the confirmation, dashboard, addresses and commodity-search pages

claims.statement: A date answer is given in one box as day/month/year text with the Ministry of Justice date picker beside it, in a ten-character-wide GOV.UK input with a small label.

classes: 'govuk-input--width-10',
    label: { text: label, classes: labelClasses },

claims.statement: A date the trader typed is read as day, month and year only when it is one or two digits, a slash, one or two digits, a slash and four digits; anything else is kept as typed and shown back to them.
claims.note: mechanism: reads and re-renders a stored { day, month, year } as d/m/yyyy text for the date picker

claims.statement: The date picker's calendar opens below the field rather than floating over the page, at most 360 pixels wide, and its toggle is a blue icon button.
claims.quote: $app-date-picker-calendar-max-width: 360px;
claims.note: extends the Ministry of Justice date picker; the mouse-focus outline on a selected day is suppressed while the keyboard focus ring is kept

claims.statement: A notification list shows its filters in a light grey panel, with a toolbar above the results that stacks below tablet width, and each result card's answers as a bold 16-pixel term over a 19-pixel value that breaks a long word rather than overflowing.
claims.note: govuk-frontend has no filter panel or result card, so the list is built from GOV.UK form groups, buttons and a description list

claims.statement: A notification list pages with a Previous and Next control at its foot rather than GOV.UK numbered pagination: a bold label with a large arrow, the page it leads to underneath in 16-pixel text, Next aligned right, and both stacked below tablet width.
A task row's status stays on one line, and a long task hint wraps instead.
claims.note: extends the GOV.UK task list

claims.statement: A table cell holding an unbroken string, such as a reference, breaks anywhere rather than pushing the table wider.
claims.note: extends the GOV.UK table

claims.statement: A total of the commodities entered is shown as a grey panel with the figure in 48-pixel bold blue, a 24-pixel bold blue label and a 19-pixel caption in the usual text colour.
claims.note: govuk-frontend has no such panel; the figure is not a GOV.UK component

claims.statement: A summary card with answers still outstanding carries a red bar down its left edge, the same red and the same bar the error summary and a field in error already use.
claims.note: extends the GOV.UK summary card, which has no error state

claims.statement: An icon button in the service is blue with a white icon, darkens on hover, and on focus takes the GOV.UK focus colour with the focus text colour, and the search icon is a white magnifier centred in a 2.5rem square.
claims.quote: $app-square-icon-button-size: 2.5rem;
claims.note: the icon is drawn as an inline SVG mask so it follows forced-colours mode

claims.statement: Previous and Next controls are shown only when a list has more than one page, with Previous left off the first page and Next off the last.
The service has no shared default page size or upper and lower bounds on one: the shared paging helper takes the page and the number of pages already worked out, so each list sets its own size.
claims.note: I looked in shared/paging.js and for every caller of pageAskedFor and previousAndNextLinks in src/. Only the notification list and the party picker page, and each passes its own size and totals; the figures themselves belong to those parts

claims.statement: A notification's pages sit under the set's own mount prefix: a page at <set>/notifications/<reference>/<page slug>, the overview at <set>/notifications/<reference>, and the set's notification list at the mount prefix itself.
claims.quote:
export const pagePath = (journeyId, slug) =>
  `${setBase()}/notifications/${journeyId}/${slug}`
export const hubPath = (journeyId) => `${setBase()}/notifications/${journeyId}`
export const createPath = () => `${setBase()}/notifications`
export const dashboardPath = () => setBase()

claims.statement: A new notification is created by posting to <set>/notifications, and a journey is entered at /start.
claims.quote:
export const createRoutePath = () => '/notifications'
export const startRoutePath = () => '/start'

claims.statement: The notification list, the create action and anything under it count as one section of the service, which is what lets the list be marked as the current navigation item.
claims.quote:
export const inDashboardSection = (path) =>
  path === dashboardPath() ||
  path === createPath() ||
  path.startsWith(`${createPath()}/`)

claims.statement: Each set of notifications is reached under its own prefix, and every URL the service builds carries it, so two sets can run side by side in the same service.
claims.note: mechanism: a set with no registered prefix is refused rather than defaulting to the root, so a wiring fault cannot hand back root URLs

claims.statement: A request is matched to its set by the longest mount prefix its path starts with, so the shared error page on a path no route answers still renders in the right set.
claims.quote:
Each set's own sandboxed `onPreAuth` enters the context for that set's
 * routes, but a request can need the context where no set route runs: the
 * shared error page on an unrouted path, and hapi-vision's marshal step

claims.statement: A set that has not configured every part of the journey platform it must configure is refused when it is mounted, named along with the call that would configure it.
claims.quote:
export const unconfiguredSeamsOf = (setId) =>
  [...requiredSeams]
    .filter(([, seam]) => !seam.has(setId))
    .map(([label, { configuredBy }]) => `${label} (${configuredBy})`)
claims.note: mechanism: wiring check at start-up, not anything a trader sees

claims.statement: Every page of a set is reached only by a signed-in user: the shared route options put every page behind the session.
claims.quote: export const routeOptions = { auth: 'session' }
